title: The Reinebold Report
subtitle: "Football is a game of leverage, angles, and finding the man who forgot to start his running back."
tagline: Week 1 — The Recap Nobody Asked For
author: Jeff Reinebold
lede: Well folks, pull up a folding chair. Week 1 is like the first day of training camp in the rain — everybody thinks they're a champion until the whistle blows and somebody's tight end lays an egg. We had fireworks, faceplants, and a man who left 51 points on his bench like loose change in a gas station parking lot. Grab a coffee. Reinebold's got the tape.

matchups.recap: Game of the Week, and it wasn't close. A league-high 161.66. The backfield of Ashton Jeanty (32.7) and D'Andre Swift (32.4) ran like they owed somebody money, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba (26.2) was open all afternoon. Bang average got a bell-cow game from Kenneth Walker III (34.1), but Jaylen Waddle (1.2) and George Kittle (3.2) showed up in invisibility cloaks.
matchups.trashTalk: You averaged 135 and still lost by 26. That's not 'bang average,' son — that's 'bring a bigger gun.' Waddle put up 1.2; I've seen more production out of the Gatorade table.

matchups.recap: Lamar Jackson (24.96) and Amon-Ra St. Brown (28.7) did the heavy lifting, with Chase Brown and Javonte Williams chipping in a combined 43. Kelce's Dream Team got a monster from Jahmyr Gibbs (33.6) and Chris Olave (28.2), but Matthew Stafford (4.1) and a 0.0 from TE Colston Loveland turned the dream into a fever nap.
matchups.trashTalk: You built a 'Dream Team' and forgot the part where the players score points. Two guys go for 60-plus and the rest napped. That's not a dream, that's a bye week.

matchups.recap: The heavyweight fight of the week. Balance from Bijan Robinson (31.3), Zay Flowers (26.0) and a clean Jalen Hurts (24.72) — nobody under 5 in the lineup. 'Champ' nearly backed up the name behind Josh Allen's absurd 35.66 and Justin Jefferson (31.2) — 67 from two guys! — but J.K. Dobbins (3.6) and a 2.0 from Brandon Aubrey left just enough on the table.
matchups.trashTalk: Hey Champ — putting the trophy in your name doesn't win the trophy. Got 67 from two studs and still couldn't close. All hat, no cattle. Keep the emoji, fix the roster.

matchups.recap: Sun God Eclipsed eclipsed the field with 156.1, riding a breakout from Christian Watson (32.7), David Montgomery (28.9) out of the FLEX, and Trevor Lawrence (26.1). Now the tragedy of the week: 'Cracked Out Uncle' scored 103.96 while leaving Isaiah Likely (27.8) and Chuba Hubbard (23.7) STAPLED to the bench — 51.5 points on the couch. Started Chargers D/ST (0.0) and Cameron Dicker (2.0) instead.
matchups.trashTalk: Uncle, I've never — NEVER — seen a man punt 51 points into his own bench. Likely and Hubbard were begging to play. Lay off whatever you're cracked out on and set your lineup, pal.

matchups.recap: Lowest-scoring affair of the week, but a W's a W. Carried by Derrick Henry's monstrous 35.3 and Trey McBride (24.5). Fittingly quiet elsewhere — Ja'Marr Chase (3.2) went silent. Major Tuddy got tidy lines from CeeDee Lamb (15.4) and Breece Hall (19.8), but the Texans D/ST posted a MINUS 4.0. Yes, negative.
matchups.trashTalk: Major Tuddy, your defense scored negative four. That's not defense, that's a hostage situation. That mascot cost you the game single-handedly.

awards.label: Stud of the Week
awards.note: Champ's QB threw the roof off. Wasted in a loss.

awards.label: Workhorse Award
awards.note: King Henry ran downhill into next Tuesday.

awards.label: Bust of the Week
awards.note: A FLEX starter worth less than a coin flip.

awards.label: Defensive Disaster
awards.note: A defense that played FOR the other team.

awards.label: Surprise of the Week
awards.note: Sun God's secret weapon torched the field.

momentOfWeek.text: Ben 'Cracked Out Uncle' Lawton leaving 51.5 points on his bench in a game he lost by 52.14. Play Likely and Hubbard and it's a nailbiter. Instead it's the beating of the week — and the most Reinebold-approved teachable moment I've got. Set. Your. Lineup.
momentOfWeek.attribution: — from the film room, Coach Reinebold

powerRankings.take: Depth for days. Sun's out, guns out.
Balanced and mean. A quiet contender.
Top-heavy. Fix the bottom of the lineup.
Won ugly. Henry carried the whole barn.
The defense cost you. Literally negative.
Benched a title. See you at lineup school.

lastWord: That's Week 1, gang. We learned Josh Allen is still Josh Allen, a defense can score negative points, and the fastest way to lose is to out-think your own bench. Set your lineups, trust your studs, and for the love of all that is holy, Uncle — start the guys who score. Reinebold out.
footerTagline: "Effort is free. So is checking your lineup."
